literal: Than dying, painful thing there is not; sweet is even that, giving not-possible time.
translation: There is nothing more painful than dying, yet even death is sweet when it is no longer possible to give to others.
modern: இறப்பதை விடத் துன்பமான செயல் வேறு எதுவும் இல்லை. ஆனால், பிறருக்குக் கொடுத்து உதவ முடியாத நிலை வரும்போது அந்த இறப்பும் இனிமையானதே ஆகும்.
explanation: The couplet contrasts the ultimate pain of death with the inability to be generous. The phrase 'சாதலின் இன்னாதது இல்லை' establishes that dying is universally considered the most painful experience. However, the poet flips this expectation by declaring that even death becomes sweet ('இனிது அதூஉம்'). This happens when one is in a state where giving to others is impossible ('ஈதல் இயையாக் கடை'). The poem emphasizes the supreme value of charity by making a life without it worse than death itself.
